Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN)  -- Authorities searched a church near where an 8-year-old California girl was found dead Monday in the hopes of finding clues that would lead to her killer. Mourners leave condolences for Sandra Cantu, who was found dead on April 6 in Tracy, California. The body of Sandra Cantu of Tracy, California, was found stuffed into a suitcase in a dairy-farm pond. Cantu had been missing since March 27. Tracy police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN's Nancy Grace he would not elaborate on what evidence led them to Clover Road Baptist Church. He would say only that detectives developed probable cause that persuaded a judge to sign a search warrant. Lane Lawless, the church's pastor, told CNN affiliate KCRA he was questioned for about three hours by police, adding that he had nothing to do with Cantu's disappearance or death. "We have fully cooperated with the police," Lawless told KCRA. "We have answered all their questions." Authorities also searched the mobile home park Tuesday where the girl lived.  Watch report on murder investigation » . "Investigators are looking at additional information they received since yesterday (Monday) and, hopefully, that will lead us to Sandra's killers," Sheneman said. Asked if his use of the plural meant police were looking for more than one person, Sheneman responded, "We have no specific suspects."  Watch Sheneman say there has not been an arrest in the case » . Sheneman also implied the killer likely was familiar with the location where the body was found. He said he himself was unfamiliar with the location where the girl's body was found, despite having lived in the community for nearly 12 years. "Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there," he said.  Watch how the suitcase was found » . Sheneman said police had no one in custody, despite having interviewed hundreds of people regarding the case. "Everyone that we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest," he said. "We're not eliminating anyone." The autopsy was being conducted Tuesday, but it was not clear when the report would be available. "It's going to be some time before we hear from the coroner," Sheneman said. "I can't tell you when that's going to be." More than 10 search warrants have been executed as part of the investigation and "a lot" of evidence has been recovered, Sheneman said. The day Cantu was last reported seen, she returned home from school, kissed her mother and left to play with a friend who lives nearby. A short time later, wearing a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings, she left to go to another friend's home, according to a family spokeswoman. Police said Monday the girl's clothing helped them identify the body.

outputs.L1:
(CNN) — Authorities searched a church near the site where an 8-year-old California girl was found dead Monday, hoping to uncover clues that could lead them to her killer.

Mourners left condolences for Sandra Cantu, whose body was discovered April 6 in Tracy, California. The girl’s body was found stuffed inside a suitcase in a dairy-farm pond. Cantu had been missing since March 27.

Tracy Police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN’s *Nancy Grace* that he would not elaborate on the evidence that led investigators to Clover Road Baptist Church. He said only that detectives had established probable cause sufficient to persuade a judge to issue a search warrant.

Lane Lawless, the church’s pastor, told CNN affiliate KCRA that police questioned him for about three hours. He added that he had nothing to do with Cantu’s disappearance or death.

“We have fully cooperated with the police,” Lawless told KCRA. “We have answered all their questions.”

Authorities also searched the mobile home park where Cantu lived on Tuesday. *Watch the report on the murder investigation »*

“Investigators are looking at additional information they received since yesterday [Monday] and, hopefully, that will lead us to Sandra’s killers,” Sheneman said.

Asked whether his use of the plural indicated that police were seeking more than one person, Sheneman replied, “We have no specific suspects.” *Watch Sheneman say there has not been an arrest in the case »*

Sheneman also suggested that the killer was likely familiar with the location where Cantu’s body was found. Despite having lived in the community for nearly 12 years, he said he was unfamiliar with the site.

“Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there,” he said. *Watch how the suitcase was found »*

Sheneman said police had no one in custody, despite having interviewed hundreds of people in connection with the case.

“Everyone that we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest,” he said. “We’re not eliminating anyone.”

An autopsy was being conducted Tuesday, although it was unclear when the report would be available.

“It’s going to be some time before we hear from the coroner,” Sheneman said. “I can’t tell you when that’s going to be.”

More than 10 search warrants had been executed as part of the investigation, and “a lot” of evidence had been recovered, Sheneman said.

On the day Cantu was last seen, she returned home from school, kissed her mother, and left to play with a friend who lived nearby. A short time later, wearing a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings, she left for another friend’s home, according to a family spokeswoman.

Police said Monday that the girl’s clothing helped them identify her body.
outputs.L2:
(CNN) — Investigators searched a church close to the location where an 8-year-old California girl’s body was discovered Monday, hoping to uncover evidence that could identify her killer.

People left messages of sympathy for Sandra Cantu, whose remains were found April 6 in Tracy, California. The child, who had been missing since March 27, was discovered inside a suitcase submerged in a pond on a dairy farm.

Tracy police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN’s Nancy Grace that he would not disclose what evidence directed investigators to Clover Road Baptist Church. He said only that detectives established probable cause sufficient for a judge to approve a search warrant.

The church’s pastor, Lane Lawless, told CNN affiliate KCRA that police questioned him for approximately three hours. He denied any involvement in Sandra’s disappearance or death.

“We have fully cooperated with the police,” Lawless said. “We have answered all their questions.”

On Tuesday, authorities also conducted a search of the mobile home park where Sandra lived. A video report covered the murder investigation.

Sheneman said investigators were examining new information received since Monday and expressed hope that it would lead them to Sandra’s killer or killers. When asked whether his use of the plural indicated that police believed multiple people were involved, he replied that investigators had no specific suspects. In a separate video, Sheneman confirmed that no arrest had been made.

He also suggested that whoever left the body probably knew the area. Sheneman said that although he had lived in the community for nearly 12 years, he had not known about the location where Sandra was found.

“Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there,” he said. Another video explained how the suitcase was discovered.

Despite interviewing hundreds of people, police had no one in custody, Sheneman said. He added that every person investigators spoke with was being treated as a person of interest and that no one had been ruled out.

An autopsy was underway Tuesday, though authorities did not know when the findings would be released.

“It’s going to be some time before we hear from the coroner,” Sheneman said. “I can’t tell you when that’s going to be.”

According to Sheneman, investigators had carried out more than 10 search warrants and collected “a lot” of evidence.

On the day Sandra was last seen, she came home from school, kissed her mother, and went outside to play with a nearby friend. A family spokeswoman said that shortly afterward, Sandra—dressed in a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings—left for another friend’s house. Police said Monday that her clothing helped them confirm the body’s identity.

### Investigators Treat Death of Sandra Cantu as Homicide  
*Tracy, California — April 2009*

Police investigating the disappearance of 8-year-old Sandra Cantu said her death was being treated as a homicide after her body was discovered inside a suitcase recovered from an irrigation pond near Tracy.

Sandra had been missing since March 27, when a neighborhood surveillance camera recorded her skipping away from the mobile-home park where she lived. Hundreds of volunteers joined law-enforcement officers in searching the surrounding area during the following ten days.

Farmworkers draining an irrigation pond several miles from Sandra’s home found the suitcase on April 6. Authorities confirmed the next day that it contained the child’s body. Investigators declined to disclose the cause of death or details about the condition of the remains, saying that releasing such information could compromise the case.

Police emphasized that the suitcase was an important piece of evidence and appealed for information from anyone who recognized it or had observed suspicious activity near the pond. Local officers were working with the FBI and other agencies, examining surveillance recordings, conducting interviews and reviewing a large number of tips. At that stage, officials had not publicly identified a suspect.

Pastor Lane Lawless of Clover Road Baptist Church, which Sandra and members of her family had attended, said the investigation had touched the congregation deeply. He described the church community as devastated and said members were cooperating with police. Lawless also confirmed that investigators had searched church property and collected material they considered potentially relevant. Contemporary accounts connected a suitcase missing from the Lawless household to the inquiry, although investigators did not initially explain publicly what significance, if any, that connection had.

Officials cautioned residents against speculation. They said detectives were interviewing people who knew Sandra and tracing her movements, but that being questioned or having property searched did not necessarily make someone a suspect.

Police also urged the public to continue submitting photographs, video and observations from the days surrounding Sandra’s disappearance. Investigators said even apparently minor details—an unfamiliar vehicle, a person carrying luggage, or activity near the irrigation pond—could help establish how Sandra was taken from her neighborhood and how the suitcase reached the water.

The discovery ended the search for Sandra but began a more focused murder investigation, leaving her family and the Tracy community waiting for an arrest and an explanation of what happened.

*This is an original, contemporaneous-style summary rather than a verbatim reproduction of a particular news article. Some early reports identified the pastor as Clifford “Lane” Lawless; quotations and precise descriptions varied by outlet.*
